chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed and Muhammad ibn Khalid Al-Barqi, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Abdul-Hamid, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding Mut'ah (temporary marriage), he said: She is not from the four (permanent wives), because she is not divorced, and does not inherit. Rather, she is only hired.

key_terms.مُسْتَأْجَرَة: Hired (referring to the nature of the contract)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal difference between a wife in Mut'ah and a permanent wife regarding inheritance and divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction of Mut'ah by categorizing the woman as 'mutajirah' (hired), thereby excluding her from the rights of inheritance and the specific mechanism of talaq (divorce) that apply to the four permanent wives. This ruling underscores the temporary, contractual nature of the union in Shia fiqh, contrasting it with the enduring familial bond of permanent marriage. The narration highlights how legal attributes are derived from the fundamental definition of the marital contract type.
